page.layout: One page of text, rotated 90 degrees on the scan. Running head at the top ("COMP. PH"). A dichotomy diagram with braces fills the page, read down the rotated lines. Top: the heading "Potentia, δυνάμεις." Below it, the first division with its branches, then the second division with its branches, then the question "Quare consideratur in" with its branches at the foot.; Running head at top, with page number at top right. Below it, one rotated block of diagram text: a bracketed outline read top to bottom, with a catchword "Ex" at the lower right. Nothing in the margins.

main_text.l: Eorum quae mutatur, quaedam mutantur secundum
Vnde totidē sunt motus species, quot sunt res secundum quas fit motus. Antequā uero aliquid moueatur, est in potētia ad actū aut
Actu, ἐντελε-χείᾳ. Horum autem aliud est

page.notes: The scan is rotated, and the diagram's braces and branch order were read from the drawing, so the levels are approximate. The Greek word in the top heading is read from a small, rotated print and may be wrong: "δυνάμεις" [?]. The line "Quare consideratur in" is followed by a bracket whose branches are the four lines below it. The line "est in potētia ad actū aut" is the end of a clause that continues in the branches "Perfectu." and "Imperfectu.". The diagram is printed sideways, so the page reads top to bottom. Nesting levels are read from the brace shapes and may be off by one. "Ex" at the lower right may be a catchword or the start of a word. The mark after "Motium." is unclear. The P of the running head is cut off by the scan edge. The page number 58 is partly faded.
